statement: The Servicemen’s Readjustment Act of 1944, called the GI Bill, was signed by President Franklin D. Roosevelt on June 22, 1944.
The GI Bill gave returning World War II veterans money for college or job training, help buying a home, and unemployment pay.
About 2.3 million veterans went to college under the GI Bill, and by 1955 it had backed 4.3 million home loans.
leaderNote: The same National Archives page notes that many Black veterans couldn’t get these loans because of discrimination. Worth a sentence if a boy asks whether everyone benefited.

statement: Today’s main version is the Post-9/11 GI Bill, which helps veterans pay for school or job training.
